title: Matched Cycle 24–25 data show a lower mean sunspot response but no clear change in short-term covariance gain
abstract: We test whether recent sunspot-index drift has the same size at short and slow time scales. We use daily SILSO V2, adjusted F10.7 and measured Bremen Mg II. We balance radio activity in cycle months 24–70. The Cycle 25 / Cycle 24 mean sunspot response above a 67 sfu radio background is 0.914 (95% 180-day block interval 0.856–0.969). The short-term covariance gain is 1.101 (0.902–1.399). Their paired contrast is 1.204 (1.014–1.521), but its 81-day block interval includes one, and a longer phase window gives 1.096 (0.920–1.292). A background-free short-to-slow gain contrast is 1.147 (0.883–2.390). This contrast is invariant to constant gains and offsets on fixed samples. The mean deficit survives activity balancing, but the time-scale evidence does not give a robust rejection of a scalar calibration change or identify a solar cause. Few blocks, proxy errors, fixed balance weights and incomplete cycles limit inference. We provide code, aggregate results, a figure and exact external input hashes. External observations remain outside the baseline bundle.

display.caption: Balanced Cycle 25 / Cycle 24 responses and the dependence of the paired contrast on the filter and block widths. Error bars are conditional 95% block intervals.
